verses.text: How terrible for those who make unfair laws, and for those who write laws that hurt people,
to take away justice from the needy and rob the poor among my people of their rights. They make widows their victims and rob orphans!
What will you do on the day of punishment, when disaster comes from far away? Who will you run to for help? Where will you leave your riches?
There will be nothing left to do but bow down among the prisoners or fall among the dead. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still raised to strike.
How terrible for Assyria, the rod of my anger! The club in its hand is my fury.
I am sending Assyria against a godless nation. I am commanding it to attack the people who make me angry, to take their goods and steal their treasure, and to trample them like mud in the streets.
But that is not what Assyria intends. That is not what it has in mind. Its plan is to destroy, to wipe out many nations.
For the king of Assyria says, "Are not all my commanders kings?
Was not Calno conquered like Carchemish? Was not Hamath like Arpad? Was not Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has taken hold of kingdoms full of idols, kingdoms whose carved images were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
I have dealt with Samaria and its idols. Shall I not do the same to Jerusalem and its idols?"
When the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will say, "I will punish the king of Assyria for the proud boasting of his heart and the arrogant look in his eyes."

For the king says, "I have done this by the strength of my own hand and by my own wisdom, because I am clever. I have moved the borders of nations and stolen their treasures. Like a mighty bull, I have brought down their rulers.

My hand has taken the riches of the nations like someone reaching into a bird's nest. Like people gathering eggs that have been left behind, I have gathered up the whole earth. Not one flapped a wing, or opened its mouth, or made a sound."

Does an axe brag that it is greater than the person who swings it? Does a saw boast against the one who uses it? That would be like a rod lifting up the person who holds it, or a wooden stick lifting up someone who is not made of wood!
So the Lord GOD of Armies will send a wasting sickness on the king's strong warriors. Under his glory a fire will be lit, burning like a blazing flame.
The Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One will become a flame. In a single day it will burn up and destroy his thorns and briers.
It will completely destroy the glory of his forests and his fertile fields, both body and soul. It will be like a sick person wasting away.
The trees left in his forests will be so few that a child could count them and write them down.
On that day the survivors of Israel, those who are left of the people of Jacob, will no longer depend on the one who struck them down. They will truly depend on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A small group will return, the survivors of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
Even though your people, Israel, are as many as the sand on the seashore, only a few will return. Destruction has been decided, and it will flood the land with righteous judgment.
For the Lord GOD of Armies will carry out the destruction he has decided on, throughout the whole land.
So this is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: "My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrians, even though they beat you with a rod and raise a club against you, as Egypt did.
In a very short time my anger against you will end, and my anger will turn to destroy them."
The LORD of Armies will beat them with a whip, as he struck down Midian at the rock of Oreb. He will raise his staff over the waters, as he did in Egypt.
On that day their heavy load will be lifted from your shoulders, and their yoke from your neck. The yoke will be broken because you have grown so strong.
The enemy has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. He stores his supplies at Michmash.
They have crossed the pass and spent the night at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has run away.
Cry out loud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is running away. The people of Gebim are running for safety.
This very day the enemy will stop at Nob. He shakes his fist at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord GOD of Armies will cut off the branches with terrifying power. The tall trees will be cut down, and the proud will be brought low.
He will cut down the thick forest with an iron axe, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
